text:
alice_support: FYI customer (Thomas at Acme Mobile) reports stream disconnects mid-response when phone switches between wifi and cellular. They get a partial JSON object and the client shows connection closed. Billing question attached — they saw a charge for what looks like a truncated response.

thomas_customer: Repro steps: open streaming chat, start generation (~40s), toggle wifi off -> cellular on. Client logs: \"stream closed by server\", last chunk is something like '{\"choices\": [ {\"delta\": {\"content\": \"... partial text\" }' then nothing. No final event.

alice_support: I grabbed their connection_id and a server-side log slice. devon, can you help triage? Customer is on our hosted API in us-west-2, traffic goes through edge-proxy cluster.

devon_oncall: Thanks. Can you paste the exact connection_id + any edge logs? Also did they use token rotation mid-request? Common pattern: client refreshes Authorization header and client reconnect logic accidentally closes existing stream.

alice_support: connection_id: conn_01F8Z9A3Y2R. Edge log snippet: \n```\n[2026-03-15T10:12:21Z] edge-proxy/1234 conn=conn_01F8Z9A3Y2R upstream=streamer-34 status=200 bytes_sent=4821\n[2026-03-15T10:12:22Z] envoy reset reason=LOCAL_RESET details=stream terminated by upstream prematurely_closed\n```\n
luis_engineer: Looks like upstream (our streamer) sent partial chunks then closed. envoy LOCAL_RESET often means the connection to backend was reset (e.g., backend process OOM, or connection pool exhausted). Can you also dump the runtime logs from streamer-34 around that time?

alice_support: Pasted runtime logs from streamer-34: \n```\n[10:12:21] generation: sending chunk seq=12 len=512\n[10:12:21] kvcache: hit=0\n[10:12:21] auth: token refresh requested for session=thomas_acme (ttl=3600)\n[10:12:22] generation: write error Broken pipe\n[10:12:22] gin: client disconnected during write\n```\n
devon_oncall: 'token refresh requested' is suspicious — if the client is performing token rotation using the same socket and then doing a silent reconnect, and the auth middleware tries to revalidate or close the session, it can race with writes. Also broken pipe indicates client closed socket or proxy closed: need to know whether client initiated FIN or we did. Can we get a tcpdump from the edge host?

thomas_customer: I can capture on the client side. Also note our mobile SDK does a background token refresh at 55 minutes and then sets a short (2s) timeout while swapping auth headers. We suspected the SDK might tear down the existing SSE connection to open a new one.

luis_engineer: That SDK behavior is the likely root cause. SSE long-lived connections are sensitive to mid-stream auth swaps. Two mitigation paths:
- Client: preemptively refresh token before a generation starts or use a refresh window where you don't swap headers mid-stream.
- Server: support token rotation via 'x-reauth' handshake or allow short-lived token refresh using a refresh-token endpoint and keep the stream alive.

devon_oncall: For immediate customer workaround, ask them to set their HTTP client socket timeout >= 30s and disable token rotation during active generations. Also enable keepalive on the client and set the SDK to send periodic comment heartbeats (e.g. ':\n') every 15s so proxies don't consider the connection idle.

alice_support: I shared a quick reproducer the engineer can run. devon, luis: please verify.

luis_engineer: Reproducer (curl):\n```\n# simple SSE client that hits our stream endpoint\ncurl -N -v \\\n  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \\\n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" \\\n  \"https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/streams/generate?model=gpt-mid\"\\n```\nIf you toggle the network interface while a long generation is streaming, you'll often see chunk followed by \"Connection closed\".

luis_engineer: Python reproducer using requests streaming:\n```\nimport requests\nr = requests.get(url, headers=headers, stream=True, timeout=90)\nfor line in r.iter_lines():\n    if line:\n        print(line)\n# on a mobile device, flip wifi off -> cellular during loop\n```\n
devon_oncall: Edge notes: we saw envoy upstream resets at ~1/5000 requests for mobile clients behind certain NATs. Proxy config recommendation: set idle_timeout slightly higher (60s -> 120s) and enable tcp_keepalive probes so intermediate NATs don't drop the mapping during handoffs. We're going to push a short-lived change to the us-west-2 edge pool to increase idle timeouts for SSE routes. deploy-bot: can you schedule?

deploy-bot: Rollout scheduled: edge-proxy/us-west-2 idle_timeout change -> 120s. Rolling update window 03:30-04:30 UTC. Will monitor.

alice_support: Customer workaround noted. Thomas: please disable SDK token rotation during active streams and try again after the rollout. Also asking finance: billing for truncated responses — how do we charge for partial streams?

finance-ops: Billing: we bill for completed tokens emitted by the model. If the stream was truncated mid-response due to network or client-side disconnect, the customer is billed only for tokens actually returned. However, if an operation was retried producing duplicate outputs, that could increase usage. We'll review Acme Mobile's invoice and flag any disputed tokens.

thomas_customer: OK will try the SDK change and report back. Appreciate the quick triage.

alice_support: Follow-ups: (1) edge rollout to increase idle_timeout, (2) create internal KB: \"SSE - midstream token rotation breakage\" describing best practices for mobile SDKs, (3) engineering follow-up to investigate graceful auth rotation support. I'll open a ticket in eng-streaming.

luis_engineer: I'll add a note to the ticket with the 'generation: write error Broken pipe' log and a request to add more telemetry: detect mid-request auth refresh, tag connection with client-sdk-version, and count partial-chunk-close events.

devon_oncall: If the customer repros after the SDK change, please attach pcap/tcpdump and connection_id. That will tell us whether the client or edge initiated the FIN.

thomas_customer: Copy that. Thanks all :thumbsup:
